arxiv-2009-08795.title: Point Forces in Elasticity Equation and Their Alternatives in Multi Dimensions
arxiv-2009-08795.creator: Q. Peng, F.J. Vermolen
arxiv-2009-08795.description: Abstract We consider several mathematical issues regarding models that simulate traction forces exerted by cells. Since the size of cells is much smaller than the size of the domain of computation, one often considers point forces, modelled by Dirac Delta distributions on boundary segments of cells.

arxiv-2107-14025.title: Addendum to ”On triangular billard”
arxiv-2107-14025.creator: Jan-Christoph Schlage-Puchta
arxiv-2107-14025.description: Abstract In [ 2 ] , the authors classified non-isosceles rational-angled triangles with the lattice property subject to the following assumption. Conjecture 1 . Let 1\leq s,t\leq n be integers such that (n,s,t)=1 . Assume that for all a with (a,n)=1 we have \frac{n}{2}<as\bmod n+at\bmod n<\frac{3n}{2} .

arxiv-2201-05466.title: Bond order via cavity-mediated interactions
arxiv-2201-05466.creator: Titas Chanda, Rebecca Kraus, Jakub Zakrzewski, Giovanna Morigi
arxiv-2201-05466.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Titas Chanda, Rebecca Kraus, Jakub Zakrzewski, Giovanna Morigi. We numerically study the phase diagram of bosons tightly trapped in the lowest band of an optical lattice and dispersively coupled to a single-mode cavity field. The dynamics is encompassed by an extended Bose-Hubbard model. Here, the cavity-mediated interactions are described by a two-body potential term with a global range and by a correlated tunneling term where the hopping amplitude depends on a global observable.

arxiv-2309-16247.title: PP-MeT: a Real-world Personalized Prompt based Meeting Transcription System
arxiv-2309-16247.creator: Xiang Lyu, Yuhang Cao, Qing Wang, Jingjing Yin, Yuguang Yang, Pengpeng Zou, Yanni Hu, Heng Lu
arxiv-2309-16247.description: Abstract Speaker-attributed automatic speech recognition (SA-ASR) improves the accuracy and applicability of multi-speaker ASR systems in real-world scenarios by assigning speaker labels to transcribed texts. However, SA-ASR poses unique challenges due to factors such as speaker overlap, speaker variability, background noise, and reverberation.

arxiv-2409-02869.title: Look Into the LITE in Deep Learning for Time Series Classification
arxiv-2409-02869.creator: Ali Ismail-Fawaz, Maxime Devanne, Stefano Berretti, Jonathan Weber, Germain Forestier
arxiv-2409-02869.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Ali Ismail-Fawaz, Maxime Devanne, Stefano Berretti, Jonathan Weber, Germain Forestier. Deep learning models have been shown to be a powerful solution for Time Series Classification (TSC). State-of-the-art architectures, while producing promising results on the UCR and the UEA archives , present a high number of trainable parameters. This can lead to long training with high CO2 emission, power consumption and possible increase in the number of FLoating-point Operation Per Second (FLOPS).

arxiv-2410-09022.title: Precessions of spherical orbits in the rotating Melvin black hole spacetime and its constraints from the jet of M87*
arxiv-2410-09022.creator: Chengjia Chen 1 , Qiyuan Pan 1,2 , and Jiliang Jing 1
arxiv-2410-09022.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Chengjia Chen 1 , Qiyuan Pan 1,2 , and Jiliang Jing 1. We investigate precessions of spherical orbits of timelike particles in the background of a rotating black hole immersed in the Melvin magnetic field, and probe effects of the magnetic field on the precession period. Our results show that effects of the magnetic field on the particles’ motions gradually decrease with the titled angle and finally vanish as the titled angle tends to π / 2 \pi/2 .

arxiv-2410-21943.title: Beyond Text: Optimizing RAG with Multimodal Inputs for Industrial Applications
arxiv-2410-21943.creator: Monica Riedler, Stefan Langer
arxiv-2410-21943.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated impressive capabilities in answering questions, but they lack domain-specific knowledge and are prone to hallucinations. Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) is one approach to address these challenges, while multimodal models are emerging as promising AI assistants for processing both text and images.

arxiv-2501-10548.title: Diffusion Models in Recommendation Systems: A Survey
arxiv-2501-10548.creator: Ting-Ruen Wei, Yi Fang
arxiv-2501-10548.description: Abstract . Recommender systems remain an essential topic due to its wide application and business potential. Given the great generation capability exhibited by diffusion models in computer vision recently, many recommender systems have adopted diffusion models and found improvements in performance for various tasks. Research in this domain has been growing rapidly and calling for a systematic survey.

arxiv-2505-12146.title: Optimal Satellite Maneuvers for Spaceborne Jamming Attacks
arxiv-2505-12146.creator: Filippos Fotiadis, Quentin Rommel, Brian M. Sadler, Ufuk Topcu
arxiv-2505-12146.description: Abstract Satellites are becoming exceedingly critical for communication, making them prime targets for cyber-physical attacks. We consider a rogue satellite in low Earth orbit that jams the uplink communication between another satellite and a ground station. To achieve maximal interference with minimal fuel consumption, the jammer carefully maneuvers itself relative to the target satellite’s antenna.

arxiv-2509-25135.title: Learning in an Echo Chamber: Online Learning with Replay Adversary
arxiv-2509-25135.creator: Daniil Dmitriev 1 Harald Eskelund Franck 2 Carolin Heinzler 2 Amartya Sanyal 2 1 University of Pennsylvania 2 University of Copenhagen
arxiv-2509-25135.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Daniil Dmitriev 1 Harald Eskelund Franck 2 Carolin Heinzler 2 Amartya Sanyal 2 1 University of Pennsylvania 2 University of Copenhagen. As machine learning systems increasingly train on self-annotated data, they risk reinforcing errors and becoming echo chambers of their own beliefs. We model this phenomenon by introducing a learning-theoretic framework: Online Learning in the Replay Setting .

pmc-10539403.title: The neglected role of abandoned cropland in supporting both food security and climate change mitigation
pmc-10539403.creator: Qiming Zheng, Tim Ha, Alexander V Prishchepov, Yiwen Zeng, He Yin, Lian Pin Koh
pmc-10539403.description: Despite the looming land scarcity for agriculture, cropland abandonment is widespread globally. Abandoned cropland can be reused to support food security and climate change mitigation. Here, we investigate the potentials and trade-offs of using global abandoned cropland for recultivation and restoring forests by natural regrowth, with spatially-explicit modelling and scenario analysis.

pmc-11691319.title: CHINESE OLDER ADULTS’ PREFERENCES FOR INVOLVEMENT IN END-OF-LIFE CARE DECISIONS: CAUSES AND OUTCOMES
pmc-11691319.creator: Yifan Lou, Jinyu Liu, Deborah Carr, Yaolin Pei
pmc-11691319.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Understanding the end-of-life decision making styles of Chinese older adults is an important goal, especially against a backdrop of global population aging. Guided by the Shared Decision-making framework, we use data from 571 adults ages 50+ in Shanghai, China to develop statistically and conceptually distinct profiles of shared, delegated, and autonomous end-of-life decision making; and identify the psychosocial and health correlates of these profiles, and the impact of profile type on advance care planning.

pmc-12537708.title: Three-dimensional gait analysis in spinal disorders: biomechanical insights and clinical applications for diagnosis, surgical planning, and rehabilitation
pmc-12537708.creator: Jun Yin, Wei Cong, Yanguo Wang, Chao Zhou
pmc-12537708.description: Three-dimensional gait analysis technology offers a novel perspective for the study and clinical application of spinal disorders, enabling a deeper understanding of patients’ movement patterns and their biomechanical characteristics. This review synthesizes the use of three-dimensional gait analysis in spinal disorders, emphasizing its significance in diagnosis, surgical planning, and rehabilitation.

pmc-12691396.title: An Alternative Treatment Effect Measure for Time-to-Event Oncology Randomized Trials
pmc-12691396.creator: Alan D Hutson, Han Yu, Vesna Zadnik
pmc-12691396.description: Simple SummaryThis work introduces a new survival analysis measure called the univariate martingale residual (UMR) for comparing treatments in phase III oncology trials. Traditional methods like hazard ratios and log-rank tests often rely on assumptions such as proportional hazards and large sample sizes, which may not hold in complex trial settings.

pmc-12757267.title: Is low-volume high intensity interval training a time-efficient strategy for improving body composition and cardiovascular health in children and adolescents? Evidence from a systematic review and three-level meta-analysis
pmc-12757267.creator: Weihua Zheng, Yue Xing, Mingyue Yin, Yan Guo, Shunzhe Piao, Yang Cao, Hongbo Chen, Hansen Li
pmc-12757267.description: ObjectivesThis meta-analysis assessed the impact of low-volume high-intensity interval training (LV-HIIT) on body composition and cardiovascular health in children and adolescents, while examining potential moderating factors.MethodsA systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library (CENTRAL), and CNKI from inception to April 2025.

pmc-13213575.title: Determining the microenvironment and protonation state of quercetin encapsulated in pillar[5]arene-based supramolecular nanocarriers
pmc-13213575.creator: Marco Milone, Martina Mazzaferro, Salvatore Patanè, Anna Notti, Ilenia Pisagatti, Giuseppe Gattuso, Norberto Micali, Valentina Villari
pmc-13213575.description: This study reports the optical properties of quercetin encapsulated in self-assembled nanoparticles made from a dicarboxyl-bis-pillar[5]arene/CTAB supramolecular complex, and correlates these properties with the nanoparticle architecture and microenvironment. Experimental evidence indicates that quercetin, in both its neutral and mono-anionic form, is mostly located within the nanoparticle, trapped between the pillararenes.

pmc-13471186.title: Perspectives on educating lifelong learning in postgraduate orthopaedic training: an interpretivist qualitative study
pmc-13471186.creator: Megan O’Connor, Jason Bantjes, Jennifer Moriatis Wolf, Leonard Charles Marais
pmc-13471186.description: BackgroundLifelong learning (LLL) is a core competency in medical education, reflecting the need for clinicians’ knowledge and skills to remain current. While postgraduate curricula emphasise LLL, a gap remains in understanding how it is interpreted and enacted within orthopaedic training.
